q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most, and their audiences are fairly happy, though mid-size channels have the happiest audiences.

- Small: 37.5% of 56 videos with a baseline outperformed (73 videos total). Net sentiment is +15 (43% positive, 28% negative, n=741 product-side comments).
- Mid: 15.6% of 32 videos outperformed. Net sentiment is +22 (48% positive, 25% negative, n=416).
- Large: 12.5% of 24 videos with a baseline outperformed (31 total). Net sentiment is +1 (38% positive, 37% negative, n=384), so opinion is split.

The small group's average lift of 6.7x is probably pulled up by a few big hits. Mid and large groups have modest sample sizes, and these are associations in a comment sample, not causes.
sql:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT c.video_id,
    CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small'
         WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid'
         WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group,
    p.outperformer, p.rel_lift
  FROM content c
  JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id
  LEFT JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id
  WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'
),
perf AS (
  SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(outperformer) AS n_with_baseline,
    ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate,
    ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift
  FROM v GROUP BY size_group
),
sent AS (
  SELECT v.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_positive,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_negative,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)-AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS net_sentiment
  FROM comments m JOIN v ON v.video_id=m.video_id
  WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor')
  GROUP BY v.size_group
)
SELECT p.size_group, p.n_videos, p.n_with_baseline, p.outperformer_rate, p.avg_rel_lift,
  s.n_product_side, s.pct_positive, s.pct_negative,
  CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN s.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment
FROM perf p LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size_group=p.size_group
ORDER BY p.outperformer_rate DESC
LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions work best for mid-sized channels. Across 13 videos, 30.8% outperformed their baseline, average relative lift was 1.68, and net sentiment was +26 (n=160 product-side comments).

Explainer/tips is a distant second: 6 videos, 16.7% outperformers, lift 1.12, net sentiment +15 (n=88).

No outperformers appeared in the other formats:
- Comparison: 3 videos, lift 0.97, net sentiment +6 (n=35).
- Upgrade advice: 6 videos, lift 0.36, net sentiment +30 (n=37). Viewers like it, but the videos underperform on views.
- Other: 3 videos, lift 0.56, net sentiment +41 (n=29).
- Keynote recap: 1 video, net sentiment -45 (n=11). That is far too small to read anything into.

Caveat: apart from first impressions, the video counts are small, and these are associations, not proof that the format caused the results.
sql: SELECT format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(CASE WHEN outperformer IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, SUM(CASE WHEN n_product_side>=10 THEN n_product_side ELSE 0 END) AS n_product_side_comments, ROUND(1.0*SUM(CASE WHEN n_product_side>=10 THEN (pct_positive-pct_negative)*n_product_side ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN n_product_side>=10 THEN n_product_side ELSE 0 END),0),3) AS net_sentiment FROM v_content WHERE topic='duo' AND format!='official' AND tier='mid 250k-1M' GROUP BY format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
The two high-lift videos with the most negative reaction are:

1. Melodie Perez's "THE IPHONE DUO IS MADE FOR CONTENT CREATORS" short. Net sentiment is -57 (14% positive, 71% negative, n=14). Lift is 591.7 (rel_lift 58.3) on about 1.56M views.

2. Man of Many's "Apple iPhone Duo Crease Test". Net sentiment is -50 (12.5% positive, 62.5% negative, n=16). Lift is 128.8 (rel_lift 12.7) on about 279K views.

UrAvgConsumer's crease video is close behind at -47 (n=19).

Lift measures reach and sentiment measures tone, so they are separate. Both samples are small (n=14 and n=16), so a few comments could shift the scores. These are also comment samples, and the link between lift and tone is an association, not a cause.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments WHERE lang='en' AND trivial=0 AND target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY video_id) SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS creator, c.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, p.outperformer, s.n_product_side, ROUND(1.0*s.pos/s.n_product_side,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(1.0*s.neg/s.n_product_side,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(1.0*(s.pos-s.neg)/s.n_product_side,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 AND s.n_product_side>=10 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, p.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 10

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
Review praise and feedback is the largest topic (n=310, 14.1% of comments), followed by Duo versus other iPhones (n=268, 12.2%) and Apple's foldable and pricing (n=231, 10.5%). Samsung Fold comparison and Plans to buy the Duo are tied at n=204 each (9.3%).

Samsung Fold comparison is growing fastest: 25 comments the prior week to 103 this week (+312%), and its share of all comments rose 3.9 points. Apple's foldable and pricing (39 to 109, +180%) and Crease and matte screen (15 to 42, +180%) come next, then Plans to buy (+176%) and Duo versus other iPhones (+149%).

Review praise nearly doubled (+98%) but lost 3.5 points of share, so it is growing more slowly than the product topics.

Multitasking and app support went from 8 to 30, but the prior-week n is small, so its growth rate was not calculated. These counts come from a comment sample.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM base), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_all, SUM(CASE WHEN d>(SELECT m FROM mx)-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wk_all, SUM(CASE WHEN d<=(SELECT m FROM mx)-7 AND d>(SELECT m FROM mx)-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pr_all FROM base), t AS (SELECT topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(CASE WHEN d>(SELECT m FROM mx)-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, SUM(CASE WHEN d<=(SELECT m FROM mx)-7 AND d>(SELECT m FROM mx)-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prior_week FROM base WHERE topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY topic_id) SELECT tp.topic_id, tp.name, tp.pool, tp.origin, tp.first_seen, t.n_total, ROUND(t.n_total*1.0/tot.n_all,3) AS share_of_all, t.n_this_week, t.n_prior_week, t.n_this_week-t.n_prior_week AS wow_change, CASE WHEN t.n_prior_week>=10 THEN ROUND((t.n_this_week-t.n_prior_week)*1.0/t.n_prior_week,3) END AS wow_growth_pct, ROUND(t.n_this_week*1.0/NULLIF(tot.wk_all,0)-t.n_prior_week*1.0/NULLIF(tot.pr_all,0),3) AS share_shift, (SELECT m FROM mx) AS latest_day FROM t JOIN topics tp ON tp.topic_id=t.topic_id CROSS JOIN tot ORDER BY t.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
a:
Duo sentiment is mildly positive at +17 net (n=1,392 comments across 129 videos), with 44% positive, 28% neutral and 27% negative.

The other topics have far fewer comments, so the comparisons are rough:
- Event general: +2 net (n=55, 6 videos), so it is more mixed than Duo. Positive is 33% and negative is 31%.
- Other: +25 net (n=28, 4 videos), slightly above Duo, but the sample is small.
- Competitor foldable: -45 net (n=11, 1 video). Only 9% are positive and 55% negative. This is one video and very small.
- iPhone 18 Pro: n=4, too few to score, so no net sentiment is reported.

Only Duo has a sample large enough to trust. These figures come from a comment sample, so treat the other topics as directional at best.
sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, COUNT(DISTINCT cm.video_id) AS n_videos, ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='positive')-AVG(cm.sentiment='negative'),3) END AS net_sentiment FROM comments cm JOIN content c ON c.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY (c.topic='duo') DESC, n_product_side DESC LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
Commenters like the Duo most when they talk about buying it and about the crease and matte screen. Criticism is milder and centres on pricing and comparisons.

Most liked:
- Plans to buy: net +35 (51% positive, 16% negative, n=186).
- Crease and matte screen: net +26 (50% positive, 24% negative, n=169).
- Under-display camera and lenses scores +37, but n=27 is small, so treat it cautiously.

Most criticised, by negative share:
- Apple's foldable and pricing: net +14 (46% positive, 32% negative, n=182).
- Samsung Fold comparison: net +9 (41% positive, 32% negative, n=99).
- Duo versus other iPhones: net +11 (41% positive, 30% negative, n=240).

No topic is net negative, so "criticised" here means the most mixed topics. These figures come from a sample of English comments on non-official videos.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT t.name AS topic_name, c.sentiment FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.target IN ('product','price_value') AND t.pool='product'), agg AS (SELECT topic_name, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS n_neg FROM base GROUP BY topic_name) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'liked' AS side, topic_name, n, n_pos, n_neg, ROUND(1.0*n_pos/n,3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*n_neg/n,3) AS neg_share FROM agg ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8) UNION ALL SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'criticised' AS side, topic_name, n, n_pos, n_neg, ROUND(1.0*n_pos/n,3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*n_neg/n,3) AS neg_share FROM agg ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8)
